beats.text: A spider wasp stung its nerve centres. It is paralysed, not killed.
She drags it into her burrow and lays a single egg on its body.
When the egg hatches, the larva feeds on the spider while it is still alive.
There are about 5,000 species of spider wasp.

caption:
Pompilidae, the spider wasps, raise their young on living tarantulas.

One precise sting to the nerve centres leaves the spider unable to move. The wasp drags it underground, attaches a single egg and closes the chamber. Some 5,000 species worldwide hunt this way.

Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.
